Underground Utility Mark-Out Before Every Grind

Before a grinder touches the ground, Ohio law requires an underground utility mark-out through the Ohio Utilities Protection Service (811). Roubic schedules the mark-out at booking as part of the job scope — there is no separate homeowner call to make. On Chagrin Falls' tight village-scale lots, where gas, water, and irrigation lines often run close to old stumps, this step protects your property and keeps the grind on schedule.

Chagrin Falls also maintains an active Shade Tree Commission overseeing the historic canopy, so if a grind is tied to removing a right-of-way or heritage tree, Roubic can flag that during the free estimate walk.

What Happens If You Defer

The Cost of Waiting — Chagrin Falls Context

Three reasons a left-behind stump costs more the longer it sits.

Sprouting & Regrowth

Many species send up suckers and new shoots from a live stump. What could have been one grind turns into repeated cutting and mowing season after season.

Pest & Decay Harborage

A rotting stump draws carpenter ants, termites, and wood-decay fungi that can move into nearby healthy trees, fences, and foundations on tight village-scale lots.

Trip Hazard & Mower Damage

Stumps in Chagrin Falls yards and along walkable downtown lots are trip hazards and blade-wreckers — a liability that only grows as grass and leaves hide them.

Common Chagrin Falls Grinding Questions

Chagrin Falls Stump Grinding FAQ

Six things Chagrin Falls homeowners want to know before booking.

How much does stump grinding cost in Chagrin Falls?
Chagrin Falls stump grinding starts at a $150 minimum per visit. Most single residential stumps (12–30 inch DBH) run $200–$450. Heritage 60-inch-plus stumps requiring the full-size track grinder run $450–$900+. Multiple-stump jobs at the same address get a per-stump discount, and a grind booked alongside a Roubic removal saves $50–$150 as a package rate.
Will Roubic grind a stump from a tree another company removed?
Yes — we routinely grind stumps from removals other contractors handled, storm-fallen trees the homeowner cleared, and stumps inherited with a property purchase. Booking is the same as any other grinding job, and the standard $150 minimum applies.
How deep does Roubic grind stumps in Chagrin Falls?
Our standard grind takes the stump 6–12 inches below grade — deep enough to plant grass, lay sod, install pavers, or pour a small concrete pad over. We can grind deeper on request if you're planning new construction or a tree replant in the same hole.
Do you handle the chip cleanup after grinding?
Yes — full chip cleanup is the default. Optional backfill with topsoil is available for an additional fee if you want the hole filled and ready for grass seed. Some customers ask us to leave the chips for use as mulch elsewhere on their property — that's free.
Do I need a utility mark-out before you grind my Chagrin Falls stump?
Yes, and Roubic takes care of it. Ohio law requires an underground utility mark-out through the Ohio Utilities Protection Service (811) before grinding. We schedule the mark-out at booking as part of the job scope — no homeowner call needed. It's especially important on Chagrin Falls' tight village-scale lots where lines often run close to old stumps.
Is Roubic licensed and insured for stump grinding in Chagrin Falls?
Yes — Roubic Tree & Landscape LLC carries full general liability and workers-compensation insurance, and has held continuous coverage since 1982. Certificates of insurance are provided on request before any work begins. We're family-owned with a 5.0 rating across Google reviews.
